findings.obs_text: In 1Ti 6:5 godliness is what the false view is about: it is taken to be a way to gain, which the verse sets in minds deprived of the truth.
findings.grounds: imagining that godliness is a means of gain

older.finding: Godliness is here the godliness, devoutness, reverence or uprightness of a person as a state of the heart toward God or toward what is right (a devout man who feared God, godliness trained and pursued, uprightness of heart, reverence and awe).
older.reason: it states a face or use of the godly words; the godly collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In 2Sa 13:33 the king is asked not to take the report to heart so as to suppose all his sons dead: the heart is where the false view would be taken up. In 1Ti 6:5 the mind of those who imagine godliness is gain is depraved: the mind is the seat of the false view.
findings.grounds: so take it to heart as to suppose

older.finding: Sequence in 2Sa 13:20–39: "do not take this to heart" → the king very angry, no act → the brother's hatred waits two years → killing → the king's spirit longs for the killer.
older.reason: it states how heart works in a person; the heart collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Act 13:25 John asks what they suppose him to be and says he is not worthy to untie the sandals of the one after him: the hearers' view of him is corrected by his own low counting of himself.
findings.grounds: What do you suppose that I am

findings.obs_text: In Act 27:13 the sailors suppose they have obtained their purpose and set sail: the supposing is about an intent reached. In Jam 4:5 purpose is in the question whether the Scripture speaks for nothing.
findings.grounds: supposing that they had obtained their purpose

findings.obs_text: In Jam 4:5 jealously names how he yearns over the spirit, the saying the readers are asked not to suppose empty.
findings.grounds: He yearns jealously over the spirit

findings.obs_text: In 2Sa 13:32 killed is the content of the view the king is not to hold, that all the young men were killed. In Act 16:27 the jailer is about to kill himself because of what he supposes: the view leads to the act against himself.

In 1Cor 8:2 the one who imagines he knows something does not yet know as he ought: the imagining is a claim to knowing that the verse sets against true knowledge. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through think; the verse sets imagining against knowing.
findings.grounds: If anyone imagines that he knows something

findings.obs_text: In Joh 11:31 the Jews suppose Mary goes to the tomb to weep, and in Joh 20:15 Mary, asked why she weeps, takes Jesus for the gardener: weeping is the setting of both supposings, and in Joh 20:15 the grief carries the mistaken view.

Dead is the content of the view in 2Sa 13:32, 2Sa 13:33 and Act 14:19: the king fears all his sons are dead and is told only Amnon is, and the crowds take Paul for dead after stoning him. In each the view is mistaken.
In Psa 41:7 the ones who imagine the worst for the psalmist are those who hate him: the devising of harm comes from hatred, with whispering together.
findings.grounds: All who hate me whisper together about me

findings.obs_text: In Pro 18:11 strong describes the city the rich man takes his wealth to be: the strength is in his own picture, a high wall in his imagination.
In Act 16:27 the jailer sees the prison doors open and from that supposes the prisoners have escaped: the sight is the ground of the view.
findings.grounds: saw that the prison doors were open

findings.obs_text: In Gen 18:29 to Gen 18:32 each case Abraham puts with suppose is followed by the Lord's answer, and in Luk 7:43 Simon answers with his view: the supposing is spoken within an exchange. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through say; the codes of answer and suppose differ in Genesis.
findings.grounds: For the sake of forty I will not do it

findings.obs_text: In Pro 18:11 wealth is what the rich man pictures as a strong city: the imagination is of what his riches are to him.
findings.grounds: like a high wall in his imagination

findings.obs_text: In Gen 18:28 righteous names the people of Abraham's case, the fifty short by five. In 1Ti 6:5 truth is what those who imagine godliness is gain are deprived of.
findings.grounds: Suppose five of the fifty righteous are lacking
